queries: Terence Tao Erdős problem solved by AI GPT-5.2 autonomously novel proof
proof LLMs cannot generalize beyond training data mathematical limitation transformers

sources_considered.why: A news report of Tao's account that GPT-5.2 Pro produced a new proof of Erdős problem #728 more or less on its own, with his caveats. Used as context showing that new outputs exist but can be read either way.

A preprint showing formal and empirical limits on transformer extrapolation for in-context learning. Context for the 'mathematically restricted' wording. Its scope is narrow and it does not cover LLMs in general.
A 2026 preprint arguing that transformers can learn rules absent from training. Found only through a search summary and not read, so not cited.
A NeurIPS 2023 paper on transformers as universal circuits for limited function classes. Similar to the arXiv context item, so not needed.

evidence_items.locator: section 'GPT-5.2 Pro cracks an Erdos problem on its own', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: Problem #728 was solved "more or less autonomously" by ChatGPT after some initial feedback, staying true to the original question without just pulling an existing solution from the literature.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows an LLM producing a proof not taken from the literature. Whether that counts as 'something new' or as 'repeating other actions' depends on a reading the speaker did not give, so this is context only.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Harder problems still need human guidance', paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: Tao estimates that only around one to two percent of currently open Erdos problems are simple enough for today's AI tools to solve with minimal human help.

evidence_items.explanation: Tao's caveat that AI wins so far come on the simpler end of open problems. This fits the speaker's broader scepticism but does not settle what 'repeating' means.

evidence_items.locator: section 4.4 Boundary values and limits of generalization

receipt.public_excerpt: This finding suggests that transformers do not learn open-ended functional rules, but instead interpolate within a bounded range tied to their training distribution.

evidence_items.explanation: A formal and empirical limit on small transformers doing in-context learning on polynomial functions. It shows that some 'mathematical restrictions' exist for narrow tasks but does not establish the speaker's general claim. Date given is the original arXiv posting; the v3 revision date was not confirmed.

unresolved_gaps: The speaker gives no definition of 'repeating other actions' or 'something new' that would separate recombination from novelty.
No formal result was found that proves or refutes a general restriction of LLMs to repeating existing actions; the formal limits found cover narrow tasks only.
